name: Moong Dal Halwa
steps: Rinse and soak moong dal for 4 hours, drain extremely well and grind to a coarse paste using as little water as possible.
Measure all ingredients and use a long-handled spatula and a heavy pan; the mixture needs frequent stirring.
Heat ghee in a heavy non-stick pan, add dal paste and stir over medium-low heat for 25–35 minutes until golden, crumbly and nutty-smelling. Do not rush this roasting.
Heat milk and water separately. Add carefully to the hot roasted dal in small additions, stirring against splashes. Cook until absorbed, then add sugar and cook for 8–10 minutes until glossy.
Stir in cardamom and any listed cashews and raisins, reserving a few for garnish. Cook gently for another 2 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes and portion into four small bowls. Serve warm; soak time, where required, is additional.
tips: Use gentle heat for milk and sugar mixtures, and scrape the base frequently to prevent scorching.
passiveTime: Allow additional soaking, resting, chilling or fermentation as specified in the steps.
notes: Quantities are for four adult portions. Cooking times are estimates; use the doneness checks in each step. Ingredient costs use sample rates and exclude unpriced items.
